primary_sources.title: Colonial Office correspondence on the War of the Golden Stool

secondary_sources.title: The Life and Times of Yaa Asantewaa of Ejisu

contested_points: Exact wording of her 1900 address varies by published account.
Birth year is often given circa 1840 but is not fixed in colonial records.
known_myths: She alone did not end British rule in Ashanti.
Popular retellings sometimes exaggerate a single battlefield outcome as total victory.

retrieval_cards.text: Ashanti leaders mobilized in 1900 to defend the Golden Stool as a symbol of sovereignty after British demands seen as humiliating.
Scholarship describes Yaa Asantewaa as Queen Mother of Ejisu who spoke in council and helped rally resistance when male leaders hesitated.
After the 1900 conflict, British authorities exiled Yaa Asantewaa and other leaders; she died in exile in 1921.
The siege of Kumasi and related fighting are documented as part of the 1900 war; outcomes were not a simple single victory for either side.
